title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: the mistery around the “Parallel Session Management” codeunit.
summary: Codeunit 490 (Parallel Session Management) is an on-premises job scheduler that fans work across multiple sessions using polling and shared memory, but its design assumptions about blocking sessions, OS-level memory sharing, and single-node architecture make it unsuitable for multi-tenant SaaS environments where Job Queue entries and async patterns are the recommended alternative.
key_points: Codeunit 490 is a manual, in-memory orchestrator using scope OnPrem procedures without async/await or platform-managed queues, with entry points like NewSessionRunCodeunit that queue jobs in temporary records and start new sessions via the platform's StartSession, throttled at 10 sessions by default

The codeunit relies on three design assumptions that work on-premises but fail in SaaS: blocking wait patterns occupy shared sessions against governance policies, OS-level memory-mapped files violate multi-tenant data isolation boundaries, and single-node scoping with ServiceInstanceId() polling breaks across distributed load-balanced nodes

WaitForAllToFinish can block a session for up to 3600 seconds polling ActiveSession every 2 seconds, which wastes shared metered resources in cloud environments and conflicts with session timeout policies

NewSessionRunCodeunitWithBlob uses shared memory segments to pass TempBlob data between sessions since they cannot share memory directly, a technique incompatible with multi-tenant isolation where customers must never access each other's data
